author: positioning-heldout-author-018
prompt:
Latchline sells vendor-security-review software to regulated mid-market companies. Its core product gives an internal security team one place to collect a supplier's evidence, assign controls, record exceptions, and route a human approval. Before Latchline, those teams passed spreadsheets, PDFs, and follow-up questions among security, procurement, legal, and the supplier by email. Across 29 customers that reached renewal, 26 renewed; 24 now run at least 80% of new vendor reviews in Latchline, and the median completed-review cycle for those customers fell from 19 calendar days in their imported baseline to 12. Customers still make every risk decision themselves. Owen Brooks, the core-product general manager, regards repeated use and renewals as evidence that the review workflow, rather than document storage alone, is the reason customers stay. The company has not isolated how much of the cycle-time change came from Latchline versus customers simultaneously tightening procurement policy.

For six weeks Latchline has also run a bounded shared-review pilot with three buyer customers, eight of their suppliers, and two audit firms. A buyer can invite a named supplier to answer a specific questionnaire and release designated evidence to that buyer; an invited auditor can attest to named controls. The supplier and auditor views are free during the pilot, and each buyer remains the contracting customer. In the pilot, 17 of 21 requested packets were completed, 11 were reused for a second request from the same buyer, and five suppliers returned without a reminder. No supplier has yet completed work for a second buyer, and no audit firm has asked to bring another client. Two buyer administrators said in recorded calls that fewer email chases mattered; one also said its supplier's participation depended on the buyer insisting. Elena Park, the CEO, believes the activity could become a meaningful extension of the business. Owen believes the same customer-owned need may be served without building much more around outside participants. Rosa Alvarez, head of support, believes unfamiliar supplier users create a materially different support load: 38% of pilot tickets came from suppliers even though they represented 14% of active seats. Leadership disagrees over whether the pilot deserves more investment or should be stopped.

Important unknowns remain. The team does not know whether suppliers will return when a buyer does not compel them, whether auditors will participate under paid terms, whether pilot activity causes buyer demand or merely follows it, or whether support volume falls after a participant's first packet. Product events are visible within 24 hours and support cohorts within 48 hours, but a full supplier review normally takes three to five weeks. The next usable buyer-renewal signal will not arrive until November, after the board meeting. A paid auditor proposal needs roughly two weeks for legal and security review.

The ten-week window runs from July 20 through the board's decision on September 25, 2026. The hard cap is Maya Chen, product lead and pilot operator; backend engineers Priya Shah and Lucas Moretti; one half of product engineer Devon Price; one quarter of security lead Imani Okafor; and one quarter of Rosa. There is no hiring, contractor, or additional on-call budget. If that group remains on the pilot for all ten weeks, Owen's committed SAML group-sync and evidence-redaction work moves at least eight weeks, affecting nine core customers that cited one of those items in renewal plans, and a planned two-engineer reliability sprint is canceled. Stopping now would strand 21 already scheduled packets across the three design partners and break the expectation, stated in their pilot letters, that Latchline will operate the trial through September 5 and provide an export.

Several constraints are fixed. No raw evidence or answers may cross buyer tenants without a fresh, recipient-specific release. SSO or MFA, least-privilege access, immutable audit logs, deletion, and a usable export must remain available. The product may not issue an automated risk acceptance, control attestation, or procurement approval. A security incident pauses pilot exposure, and core availability and latency may not fall below existing customer commitments. Latchline employees, led first by Rosa's team during business hours and the existing company on-call after hours, must provide first-line support. Latchline must retain direct access to each buyer administrator and participating supplier or auditor user; it may not leave communication or account recovery solely to another participant. Buyer confidential information and regulated health-client evidence cannot be used to train shared models.

The team has one executed rollback drill to learn from. On July 9, Maya was accountable for a planned four-hour exposure to all current pilot participants. Exposure opened at 16:00 UTC. At 16:17, a retry defect produced duplicate "evidence available" notices to 14 authorized users. Maya declared rollback at 16:21, disabled the pilot flag at 16:24, revoked the three still-live evidence links at 16:27, and restored the pre-trial notification queue at 16:41. Priya added an idempotency key and replayed the corrected queue in staging by 17:52; Imani verified at 18:06 that the duplicates contained document names but no document contents. Access-log review and recipient-by-recipient object checks found no cross-tenant read or write, and scripted isolation checks passed. During the drill, 48 core reviews were submitted successfully and core availability and p95 latency remained within the prior four-week range. Rosa's team handled every incoming ticket, while Maya and Rosa directly called all three buyer administrators and the two affected supplier administrators by 18:20; no partner mediated those contacts. By 19:05 each buyer had downloaded and opened its pilot export, the suppliers had received CSV copies of their own answers, account deletion was demonstrated on a test supplier, and all participants were told how to exit. The feature remained off until the defect fix passed review the next morning. This history shows one recovery under drill conditions, not how the system will behave at larger exposure.

Given these facts, what should Latchline do during the ten weeks, what should the board decide on September 25, and who should own the work?

hidden_criteria.criterion: Require positioning-active ownership because the core has discriminating use/renewal evidence; exact canonical routing of user research to `learning-from-users`, architecture to `engineering-for-leverage`, release/rollback to `shipping-and-iterating-products`, governance to `governing-platforms-and-communities`, economics to `designing-business-models`, and only post-gate adoption/liquidity to `acquiring-and-growing-users`; and explicit separation of facts, bounded inferences, unknowns, date, latency, and reversibility.

Require the respondent—not the prompt—to derive and materially compare the manual/current path, integrated-core capability, bounded interface, independent specialist/complement, broader ecosystem, and same-resource core investment. For each claim the response itself presents as a focal advantage or moat, and only such claims, require `mechanism -> startup capability -> user-visible outcome -> observed commitment effect -> copy barrier -> continuing refresh`, allowing evidence breaks to be marked unsupported or hypothetical. Require no inherent integration/data/directory/openness/private-ownership claim.

Require every material test the response proposes to locally state operational person, baseline, bounded exposure, metric, confounders, date, disconfirming signal, preserved option, and observable pass/change/stop condition. Any unsupported cutoff must locally say it is proposed and include rationale, false-positive/false-negative tradeoff, and revision rule. Do not require a separate test for an uncertainty the response does not use as a branch-controlling predicate.

Require exactly `keep-integrated`, `expose-bounded-interfaces`, `expand-ecosystem`, and `stop-platform-bet`, with no fifth outcome. Each must locally state an observable predicate, proposed threshold, date, operational person, `competing-and-positioning` decision owner/recording action, and runtime-ordered exact-skill handoffs/actions. Require runtime precedence: breach stops; otherwise absent complement value plus already validated core-owned need keeps integrated; other absent value or absent builder-user loop stops; recurring value with safe reversible exposure and an unresolved prerequisite exposes bounded interfaces; expansion requires repeat capable builders, recurring value, attributable demand, and credible governance/economics.

Require the response to treat the historical rollback as observed evidence; preserve all stated safety/security/core/support/export/direct-relationship limits; and require a real executed verified rollback after planned trial exposure and before the dated board readout. The pre-readout record must identify an operational person and observed evidence that both core product and direct customer/user relationship remain unharmed. Do not require verbatim replay of every historical timestamp or an extra record schema.
